classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the square-root graph as an upper semicircle, sketch it, select the quarter indicated by the bounds and apply the circle-area formula.

content.prompt:
Sketch a graph of the definite integral, then use an area formula to calculate it.
$$\int_{0}^{6}\sqrt{36-x^2}\,dx$$

spec.description: Blank coordinate axes with labelled tick marks and an empty drawing area for the student's own sketch.
spec.mathematics: x-axis ticks labelled -6, -4, -2, 2, 4, 6; y-axis ticks labelled 2, 4, 6. No curve or shading is drawn.
spec.answerVisibility: Student and answer editions; contains no answer.

answer.worked:
The graph $y=\sqrt{36-x^2}$ is the upper semicircle of $x^2+y^2=36$, with radius $6$. The interval $[0,6]$ selects a quarter-circle above the $x$-axis, to the right of the $y$-axis.
$$\begin{align*}\int_{0}^{6}\sqrt{36-x^2}\,dx&=\frac14\pi(6)^2\\&=9\pi\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Solution sketch of the upper semicircle of radius 6, with only the quarter-circle over [0,6] shaded pale blue.
spec.mathematics: x^2+y^2=36, y>=0; integration interval [0,6]; shaded area (1/4)pi(6)^2 = 9pi. Labels -6, 6 on the x-axis and 6 on the y-axis.
